take_homes: The cheapest control is not granting the access. Every door left closed is a risk nobody has to sign for, and it costs a feature.
An agent can be steered by a document it reads, so the control is limiting what it can read and change and who reviews its output, not trusting it.
Going from prototype to production means working through every risk on the list, not one. I'd want to see that cost before agreeing to anything.

monday.move: Ask IT and the controller which finance data any AI tool can see today, and ask whether anyone has done an access review.
monday.stop_condition: IT says it's already covered and shows me the review.
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data, and I can't run the skill myself.

misconception.why: I still don't know what any of this costs. But 'every risk must be controlled before production' means a licence alone isn't enough, and the organisation has to build the controls.

one_line: Two or three solid ideas, like closing doors and signing for the residual, buried in a lot of filler. Nothing in it has a cost, a payback or a number to take to the board.
